title: Kabul retirees protest unpaid pensions
organizer: Retired public employees; formal organizer not reported.
participants_original: TOLOnews search preview says “dozens” of retired officials; AAN describes a group of pensioners. Neither gives a count that verifies 50 or more.
threshold_50_evidence: The only opened report says a group attended; the TOLOnews search preview says “dozens.” This does not establish 50 or more. Keep the candidate pending threshold; do not convert “dozens” to a numeric range.

start_date.summary: AAN dates a group pensioners’ demonstration in Kabul to 2 January 2023.

location.summary: Both records place the gathering in Kabul; no exact site is established.

organizer.summary: Participants are described as retired officials or pensioners; no named formal organizer is given.

demands.summary: TOLOnews search preview says protesters criticized unpaid pensions and called on the Islamic Emirate to pay them.

participants_original.summary: TOLOnews search preview says “dozens”; AAN says a group. No exact attendance estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: “Dozens” and “a group” do not verify a minimum of 50.

end_date.summary: No physical end or last day of protest activity is reported.

protester_violence.summary: The accessed passage does not describe violence; silence is retained as unknown.

state_response.summary: AAN reports a Finance Ministry spokesman later telling TOLOnews that about AFN 4 billion was allocated for retirees pending approval, but neither account ties this statement to a meeting, agreement or direct response to this gathering. All seven response fields remain unknown.

state_target.summary: The only reported demand to the Islamic Emirate is in the TOLOnews search preview; the opened AAN report does not independently establish what the gathering demanded.

notes: Candidate only. “Dozens” in the TOLOnews search preview does not establish whether attendance met the threshold. The reported call on the Islamic Emirate to pay pensions is available only in that search preview; AAN describes a Kabul pensioners demonstration but does not establish its demand or state target. TOLOnews body retrieval failed technically, not through an access denial. AAN cites TOLOnews for the event/statement and is not independent confirmation of crowd details. Do not infer an end or direct government response.
open_questions: Can any accessible source verify whether 50 or more attended?
Can the full TOLOnews text or another independent report verify that the gathering demanded payment from Afghanistan’s authorities?
What was the exact site and physical end?
Was the Finance Ministry statement a direct response to the gathering?

title: Badakhshan Friday protest after Quran burning in Sweden
location: Badakhshan Province; exact city/site not reported
organizer: Unknown; no organizer for this local gathering is identified.
participants_original: A Badakhshan provincial-government spokesperson told Reuters that thousands gathered after Friday prayers. Keep the source wording; no exact number is reported.
threshold_50_evidence: The provincial-government spokesperson’s report of thousands at the Badakhshan gathering exceeds the project threshold, but it is not an exact count. Do not derive a precise minimum or maximum.

start_date.summary: The Reuters article was published 28 January and says the gathering occurred Friday, 27 January; Afghanistan International dates its account to 7 Dalw 1401 (27 January).

location.summary: Reuters reports thousands gathered in Badakhshan after Friday prayers; the exact city/site is missing. Afghanistan International includes Badakhshan in a province list attributed to Bakhtar.

organizer.summary: The Reuters report does not identify an organizer for the Badakhshan gathering. CIR describes Taliban-linked mobilization in the wider series but does not establish centralized organization of this event; Afghanistan International attributes its province list to Taliban-controlled Bakhtar.

demands.summary: The spokesperson says participants chanted “Death to Sweden, U.S.A and U.N” and also asked the Islamic Emirate to take a strong position against such acts. Preserve both the foreign-target slogans and explicit domestic-government request.

participants_original.summary: Reuters quotes a Badakhshan provincial-government spokesperson reporting thousands gathered after Friday prayers.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The Badakhshan-specific report says thousands, but supplies no exact number.

end_date.summary: The reports do not state a physical end for this Badakhshan gathering. Do not use the wider protest series end or report date as its end.

protester_violence.summary: The accessed reporting does not establish violence at this Badakhshan gathering; retain unknown.

state_response.summary: Reuters says the Afghan Foreign Ministry had condemned the Quran burning earlier that week; CIR reports a condemnation on 29 January. Neither source establishes these statements as a response to or accommodation of this gathering. All seven response fields remain unknown.

notes: Preserve as pending_state_target. The Reuters account attributes both foreign-target slogans and a request directed to Afghanistan’s Islamic Emirate. Coordinator review must decide whether this meets the codebook’s home-grown/state-target rule. S005 is a Reuters report republished by Euronews; its Reuters origin was identified only after the article was opened. S010 repeats Bakhtar-attributed provincial coverage and is not independent evidence for the Badakhshan count.
open_questions: Does the explicit request to Afghanistan’s Islamic Emirate satisfy the domestic state-target rule when slogans also target foreign/international actors?
What was the exact city/site and organizer?
What was the physical end, if any, and which government actions directly responded to this gathering?

title: Herat Cinema Square gathering after Quran burning in Sweden
organizer: Unknown for the Herat gathering. Etilaatroz describes the wider protests as Taliban-coordinated but names no local organizer.
participants_original: Etilaatroz reports “hundreds” across Balkh, Herat, Ghor and Badghis collectively; it gives no Herat-specific count.
threshold_50_evidence: The article identifies a Herat gathering at Cinema Square but allocates no part of the four-province aggregate “hundreds” to Herat. It cannot establish 50 at this site.

start_date.summary: Etilaatroz dates the demonstrations to Friday, 27 January 2023.

location.summary: The account locates Herat slogans and Swedish-flag burning at Cinema Square.

organizer.summary: Etilaatroz attributes coordination to the Taliban generally but does not identify a local Herat organizer.

demands.summary: The report says protesters called for punishment of those responsible but names no addressee; it quotes “Death to Sweden and enemies of Islam.” Preserve both the unspecified punishment demand and foreign-target slogans.

participants_original.summary: “Hundreds” is an aggregate for four provinces and is not allocated to Herat.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No site-level number is reported for Cinema Square; the four-province total cannot be allocated to this gathering.

end_date.summary: No physical end or last day of Herat protest activity is reported.

protester_violence.summary: The accessed article does not establish protester violence at the Herat gathering; retain unknown.

state_response.summary: The article does not establish a direct response to this gathering; all seven response fields remain unknown.

notes: Keep the addressee of “punishment” and the Cinema Square threshold unresolved. The reported slogans target Sweden and “enemies of Islam”; the article does not identify an Afghan state recipient. Do not merge with Badakhshan or allocate the four-province aggregate to Herat.
open_questions: Who, if anyone, was the addressee of the call to punish those responsible?
Did 50 or more gather at Cinema Square?
What was the physical end and any direct state response?

participants_original.summary: CIR describes “several hundred” participants in Kandahar.

end_date.summary: No physical end for the Kandahar event is reported.

title: Mazar-e-Sharif gathering after Quran burning in Sweden

participants_original: Etilaatroz describes “dozens” in Mazar-e-Sharif. This wording has no numerical upper bound and does not establish whether 50 or more attended.
threshold_50_evidence: The source says “dozens” but gives no number or upper bound. Threshold status is unverified; do not code the gathering as below 50 or as meeting 50.

start_date.summary: Etilaatroz reports the Mazar-e-Sharif gathering in its 27 January 2023 account.

location.summary: The article identifies Mazar-e-Sharif but gives no precise site.

organizer.summary: The report attributes coordination to the wider Taliban-led protests and says sources described pressure on Mazar shopkeepers; no distinct formal local organizer is identified.

demands.summary: No demand or addressee is separately attributed to the Mazar gathering. The article’s broader call for punishment of Quran-burning perpetrators is not assigned to Mazar.

participants_original.summary: The source uses “dozens” for Mazar-e-Sharif; no exact number or upper bound is supplied.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: “Dozens” alone does not determine whether attendance was below or at least 50.

end_date.summary: No physical end or last date of Mazar activity is reported.

protester_violence.summary: The accessed article does not establish protester violence at the Mazar gathering; retain unknown.

state_response.summary: The article does not establish a direct state response to the Mazar gathering; all seven response fields remain unknown.

notes: Keep this as an unresolved local lead, not a below-50 exclusion. “Dozens” has no verified upper bound; the report provides no Mazar-specific demand/addressee. Do not import the four-province aggregate count or Herat slogans into this gathering.
